definition: A retrieval technique that generates several variations of a user's query (often using an LLM) and combines the retrieved results from each, to improve overall retrieval coverage.
details: Multi-query retrieval helps counteract the sensitivity of embedding-based search to exact query phrasing, casting a wider net across semantically related reformulations of the original question.
story: Imagine a driving test that every new model has to pass before it is allowed on the road. In plain words: A retrieval technique that generates several variations of a user's query (often using an LLM) and combines the retrieved results from each, to improve overall retrieval coverage. Here is how it actually plays out: Multi-query retrieval helps counteract the sensitivity of embedding-based search to exact query phrasing, casting a wider net across semantically related reformulations of the original question. It is the exam that keeps everyone honest. That shared ruler is Multi-Query Retrieval.
